organic:oc-1k5glo1.w: Its central CH2 sits between two carbonyls, so mild base removes one of those hydrogens selectively and the resulting enolate, stabilized by both carbonyls, is the nucleophile.
s: Find the most acidic H: on the CH2 **between the two C=O** groups.
Its pKa is about 11, far below a simple ketone's 20.
Mild base removes it: an enolate shared by **both carbonyls**.
That carbon is the **nucleophile** in the aldol step.
t: Dehydration can only happen after the C-C bond has formed and there is an OH to lose.
The ester oxygen has no hydrogen to remove. The acidic hydrogens are on the central carbon.
A base cannot reduce a ketone. Reduction needs a hydride source.
It does have alpha hydrogens: two of them, on the CH2 between the carbonyls, and they are the most acidic in the molecule.
c: Roughly what is the pKa of the CH2 hydrogens in ethyl acetoacetate?
About 11.

organic:oc-1bxsg2d.w: The product is 1-bromo-4-methylpentane. With peroxides the bromine atom adds first, to the end carbon, because that leaves the more stable secondary radical; hydrogen then caps that radical.
s: Peroxides make **bromine atoms**: a radical chain.
Br adds to the **end CH2**, leaving a secondary radical.
That radical takes an H from HBr.
Br is on the terminal carbon: **anti-Markovnikov**.
t: Two bromines is what Br2 gives. HBr adds one H and one Br.
Bromine on C2 is the Markovnikov product, formed when no peroxide is present.
This puts Br on C3. Radicals do not rearrange, and neither alkene carbon is C3.
A tertiary bromide would need the reactive center to migrate down the chain. Radical additions do not rearrange.
c: Does the peroxide effect work with HCl or HI?
No. Only HBr adds anti-Markovnikov with peroxides.

organic:oc-75v5a0.w: The product is the methyl ester with the stereocenter unchanged: methyl (S)-2-phenylpropanoate. Methanol attacks the carbonyl carbon and chloride leaves; the neighboring stereocenter is never involved.
s: Methanol attacks the **carbonyl carbon**.
Chloride leaves: an acid chloride becomes an **ester**.
No bond to the stereocenter is made or broken.
Its configuration is **retained**.
t: This is drawn with no stereochemistry, as if the center had been scrambled. Nothing touches it, so it stays (S).
This is the inverted configuration. Inversion needs backside attack at the stereocenter, and the reaction is at the carbonyl carbon.
This is the ethyl ester. Methanol supplies a methyl group.
The carboxylic acid would need water as the nucleophile. The reagent is methanol.
c: What is the other product of this reaction?
HCl.

organic:oc-1cv6f2u.w: Acetaldehyde and benzaldehyde. Ozonolysis cuts the C=C; each alkene carbon has one hydrogen, so each becomes an aldehyde, and the zinc workup leaves them as aldehydes.
s: **Cut the C=C** and put an O on each carbon.
The methyl side has one H: **acetaldehyde**.
The phenyl side has one H: **benzaldehyde**.
Zinc and water keep both as **aldehydes**.
t: Propanal has three carbons. The methyl side of the alkene has only two.
The two acids are what an oxidizing workup (H2O2) gives.
Formaldehyde and acetophenone would come from 2-phenylpropene, which has a =CH2 end.
Formaldehyde and benzaldehyde would come from styrene. Here the far alkene carbon carries a methyl.
c: What does 2-methyl-2-butene give with O3, then Zn?
Acetone and acetaldehyde.

organic:oc-1cv2c5c.w: Acetone comes over first. In a distillation the liquid with the lowest boiling point vaporizes first, and 56 C is well below 100 C and 111 C.
s: Distillation separates by **boiling point**.
The lowest boiling liquid **vaporizes first**.
Compare: 56, 100 and 111 C.
**Acetone**, at 56 C, is collected first.
t: Toluene has the highest boiling point of the three, so it comes over last.
The stem rules out azeotropes, so the components leave in order of boiling point.
Water boils at 100 C, well above acetone, so it comes over second.
Molar mass does not set the order. Water is the lightest molecule here and still boils 44 degrees above acetone.
c: When is fractional distillation needed instead of simple distillation?
When the boiling points are close, within about 25 C of each other.

organic:oc-1fhb3ww.w: The arrow runs from the negatively charged ylide carbon to the carbonyl carbon. The ylide carbon is the nucleophile and the carbonyl carbon is the electrophile.
s: An ylide has a **carbon with a negative charge** next to P+.
That carbon is the **nucleophile**.
The carbonyl carbon is the **electrophile**.
Arrow: from the ylide carbon to the carbonyl carbon, a new **C-C bond**.
t: The carbonyl oxygen bonds to phosphorus later. It does not attack the ylide carbon, which is already electron-rich.
The aldehyde C-H bond is not broken in a Wittig reaction.
Phosphorus in an ylide is positive and has no lone pair to give.
The C=O pi electrons end up on oxygen. The P-O bond forms after the C-C bond.
c: What are the two final products of a Wittig reaction?
An alkene and triphenylphosphine oxide.

organic:oc-1gnnsax.w: Two pi electrons, aromatic. The one C=C supplies two pi electrons, the positive carbon supplies an empty p orbital that completes the ring of overlap, and 2 fits 4n+2 with n = 0.
s: One C=C: **2 pi electrons**.
The cation carbon has an **empty p orbital**: 0 electrons.
All three carbons are sp2: a full ring of p orbitals.
2 = 4n+2 with **n = 0**: aromatic.
t: The double bond holds two pi electrons, so the count is not zero.
Four would be the cyclopropenyl anion, which has a lone pair in the ring. The cation has an empty orbital.
The count is right, but 2 is a 4n+2 number. Antiaromatic rings have 4n.
Six would need three pi bonds or lone pairs. A three-carbon ring with one C=C has two.
c: Is the cyclopropenyl anion aromatic?
No. It has 4 pi electrons, a 4n count, so it is antiaromatic.

organic:oc-mnw0d4.w: The product is cis-cyclopentane-1,2-diol. Permanganate delivers both oxygens to the same face of the double bond in one step, so the two OH groups are cis.
s: Cold, dilute KMnO4 adds **two OH** groups.
Both oxygens come from one MnO4 unit: **same face**.
On a ring, same face means **cis**.
The cis diol has a mirror plane: it is meso.
t: This is the trans diol. It comes from opening an epoxide with water, not from permanganate.
The epoxide is what a peroxyacid such as mCPBA gives.
Cyclopentanol has one OH. That is hydration, not dihydroxylation.
The hydroxy ketone is an over-oxidation product. Cold, dilute conditions stop at the diol.
c: Name another reagent that gives the same cis diol.
OsO4 (with NaHSO3 or NMO).

organic:oc-qjs2wp.w: The reaction is extremely slow. Iodide in acetone reacts by SN2, and although the carbon holding bromine is primary, the tert-butyl group next to it blocks the backside approach.
s: NaI in acetone: **SN2** conditions.
SN2 needs room behind the C-Br bond.
The next carbon carries **three methyls** that block that path.
Primary, but hindered: SN2 is **very slow**.
t: Acetone is not a base, and the neighboring carbon is quaternary, so there is no hydrogen there to remove.
A primary cation is too unstable to form, and acetone is a poor solvent for ionization.
Primary usually means fast SN2, but branching on the neighboring carbon blocks the backside. Neopentyl is the standard exception.
The neighboring carbon is quaternary: it has no hydrogen to shift. And no cation forms under these conditions.
c: Which reacts faster with NaI in acetone: 1-bromobutane or neopentyl bromide?
1-Bromobutane, by a factor of many thousands.

organic:oc-17mk9ys.w: The product is 6-oxoheptanal. Ozonolysis cuts the ring C=C and opens the ring: the methyl-bearing carbon becomes a ketone, the CH carbon becomes an aldehyde, and dimethyl sulfide leaves the aldehyde as it is.
s: **Cut the C=C**; put an O on each carbon.
The double bond is in the ring: the **ring opens**.
The methyl carbon has no H: a **ketone**.
The other carbon has an H: an **aldehyde**, kept by Me2S.
t: Heptane-2,6-dione makes both ends ketones. The alkene carbon with an H gives an aldehyde.
1-Methylcyclohexanol is a hydration product. Ozone cleaves the double bond.
Heptanedial makes both ends aldehydes. The methyl-bearing carbon has no H, so it must be a ketone.
The keto acid is what an oxidizing workup (H2O2) gives. Dimethyl sulfide is a reducing workup.
c: Which workup reagents keep aldehydes as aldehydes?
Zinc with acetic acid or water, or dimethyl sulfide.

organic:oc-xtm96d.w: H2 with Lindlar's catalyst. The poisoned palladium adds one H2 to the same face and stops at the cis alkene.
s: Goal: alkyne to **cis alkene**, and stop.
Cis needs both H on the **same face**: a metal surface.
Stopping needs a **poisoned** catalyst.
That is **Lindlar's catalyst**.
t: Raney nickel with excess H2 is very active and reduces all the way to the alkane.
Ordinary Pd/C does not stop at the alkene. It gives butane.
Sodium in liquid ammonia stops at the alkene but gives the trans isomer.
Adams' catalyst is an active platinum catalyst and reduces through to the alkane.
c: Which reagent gives the trans alkene from an internal alkyne?
Sodium (or lithium) in liquid ammonia.

organic:oc-dp6bvf.w: The product is 3-methylcyclopent-2-en-1-one. The enolate of one end methyl attacks the other carbonyl to close a five-membered ring, and loss of water gives the conjugated enone.
s: Base makes the enolate at an **end CH3**.
It attacks the other C=O: C1 through C5, a **five-membered** ring.
The aldol product loses **water**.
C=C next to C=O, methyl on the alkene carbon.
t: This ring carries two methyl groups: seven carbons. The diketone has only six.
Cyclopentane-1,2-dione has five carbons and no methyl. All six carbons must appear in the product.
The C=C here is not next to the C=O. Dehydration gives the conjugated enone.
A product with two carbonyls has not lost water. An aldol condensation ends with one C=O and one C=C.
c: Why does the enolate form at the end methyl and not at an inner CH2?
Attack from an inner CH2 would close a strained three-membered ring. The methyl enolate closes a five-membered one.

organic:oc-1jgftmx.w: The major alkene is 2,3-dimethyl-2-butene. Loss of water gives a secondary cation next to a quaternary carbon, a methyl shifts to make a tertiary cation, and loss of a proton gives the tetrasubstituted alkene.
s: Protonate OH, lose water: a **secondary** cation.
The neighbor is quaternary: a **methyl shifts** over.
Now a **tertiary** cation.
Lose the neighboring H: the **tetrasubstituted** alkene (Zaitsev).
t: This is an alkyl chloride. There is no chloride in the flask, and the question asks for an alkene.
This alkene has seven carbons. The alcohol has six.
3,3-Dimethyl-1-butene is the unrearranged alkene. The cation rearranges before it loses a proton.
This is an alkane. Dehydration removes water; it does not add hydrogen.
c: Why does a methyl shift here instead of a hydride?
The neighboring carbon is quaternary and has no hydrogen to give.

organic:oc-1nni7r4.w: Water with H2SO4 and HgSO4. The data describe a methyl ketone (C=O near 1715, CH3 singlet near 2.1, no CHO proton), which is the Markovnikov hydration product of a terminal alkyne.
s: 1715 cm-1: a **ketone** C=O.
3H singlet at 2.1 ppm: **CH3 next to C=O**.
No signal at 9 to 10 ppm: **not an aldehyde**.
Methyl ketone from a terminal alkyne: **Markovnikov hydration**, Hg(II) and acid.
t: Disiamylborane then peroxide is anti-Markovnikov. It gives the aldehyde, which would show a proton near 9 to 10 ppm.
Hydroboration puts the oxygen on the end carbon and gives an aldehyde, not a methyl ketone.
Ozonolysis cuts the triple bond. It would give a carboxylic acid, with no CH3 singlet.
Lindlar reduction gives an alkene. There would be no carbonyl band.
c: Which reagents turn this alkyne into an aldehyde?
Disiamylborane (or 9-BBN), then H2O2 and NaOH.

organic:oc-17kba84.w: The product is (E)-3,4-dibromo-3-hexene, with the two bromines on opposite sides of the double bond. One Br2 adds anti across the triple bond and the reaction stops at the alkene.
s: One equivalent of Br2 adds **one Br to each** alkyne carbon.
The product is a **dibromoalkene**.
Anti addition: the two Br are on **opposite sides**.
On each carbon Br outranks ethyl, so opposite sides is **E**.
t: This has three bromines and no double bond. One Br2 supplies only two bromines.
Two bromines on one carbon with no C=C is what two equivalents of HBr would give.
This has no double bond and one Br per carbon. That would need hydrogen added as well.
This is the Z isomer, with both bromines on the same side. Anti addition puts them on opposite sides.
c: What forms with two equivalents of Br2?
3,3,4,4-Tetrabromohexane.
